summary: Diagnose why 37 void-lot orgs survive refold-void-names drains: the walk lists them, the fold retires 0 of their mentions

diagnoses.root_cause:
The walk and the fold don't apply the same rule. The walk tests one name. The fold tests the whole party.

- **Walk.** It decides whether to re-queue by running `is_void_lot` on `organizations.name` alone. That is the head name, the party's first-seen copy (crates/app/src/supervisor.rs:3794, applied at :5581; crates/store/src/canonical.rs:19185 reads only that column). The doc comment says it splits "by the fold's own rule", but `is_void_lot` is the fold's rule for a single name, not its rule for a party.
- **Fold.** `drop_decision` collects every published name copy of the party section (crates/ingest/src/project.rs:4522-4538; the name fields at :862 are TED-OFFICIALNAME, TED-ORGANISATION and TXT-AU). It drops the party only in two cases:
  - every copy is classed as a non-name (:4548), or
  - there are at least 4 copies and at least half are void (:4556).
  Otherwise it hits `continue` and keeps the party (:4559).
- **No void echo.** Neither echo pass rescues these parties. `translation_echoes` and `template_echoes` (:4540) only spread the Placeholder class, never VoidLot.
- **Lexicon coverage.** `VOID_WHOLE` (crates/ingest/src/partyname.rs:141-195) holds one TED wording per language, matched whole. These notices use other TED wordings, for example 'Zuschlag nicht vergeben', 'Kontrakten ikke tildelt.', 'Der Auftrag wurde nicht vergeben.', 'Partiet blev ikke tildelt', 'Los wurde nicht vergeben' and 'Lote no adjudicado'. They read as names, so only 1-7 of each party's 23-24 copies count as void, and the 2-copy IT/DE party has one unclassed copy.

So the fold keeps all of these parties. `retire_mentions` (project.rs ~3459) only receives sections the fold dropped, so nothing is retired. That matches project 2353 on the box: 0 non-name retired, and only 2 void drops (parties with no recorded mention left).

There is a second, smaller difference: case. `void_prefix` treats a lowercase next word as part of the void phrase (partyname.rs:2500). So 'No award was made' reads VoidLot, but the all-caps 'NO AWARD WAS MADE' reads as a name. The walk reads the org's mixed-case head; the fold reads the notice's all-caps copy.

The fold's retire path is not at fault. It is never handed these sections.

diagnoses.explains:
I located 39 of the 40 mentions (25 of the 26 notices) using public GETs: `/v1/organizations?name_prefix=`, `/v1/tenders?winner=`, `/v1/notices?tender=` and each notice's `/content`.

**Multi-copy parties: 38 mentions on all 24 r208 notices.** The head copy is void, but the other copies are unclassed, so the fold keeps the party.
- 7 mentions are bilingual IT/DE: 'non aggiudicato' / 'Zuschlag nicht vergeben'. There are 5 on 12501289 and 2 on 4416766 (orgs 31408169/70). These have 2 copies, so the majority rule never applies.
- 31 mentions carry TED's 23-24-language templates:
  - 'Marché non attribué.' on 16893864 ORG-2..5: 6 of 23 copies void.
  - 'Lot not awarded': 4 of 23-24 void.
  - 'No contract awarded' and 'Contract not awarded': 5-7 void.
  - 'Ce lot est infructueux.': 2 void.
  - 'Procédure infructueuse': 2 void.
  - 'Aucune offre reçue': 1 void.
  - 'Non-attribution du marché': 3 void.
  - The 'Non applicable — …' family (6709213's 4 mentions on 18344075, 7400280, 6023876, 7969717): 2 void, and the EN/PL copies class as Blank.

**Case: 1 mention, the one text notice.** On 3322691, ORG-2 is published as 'NO AWARD WAS MADE', which `not_a_name` reads as a name (None). The mention binds to org 27220329, whose head is 'No award was made' (VoidLot). The walk lists it; the fold keeps it.

**Not located: 1 mention, the one r209 notice.** Org 1265984 'marché déclaré sans suite' (country FR) has no winner, buyer or bidder tender in the public API, and the box SQL read was denied. Its head name alone reads VoidLot, so it is probably the multi-copy shape again, but I have not confirmed that.

The 37 orgs and 40 mentions in total match the dry report.
diagnoses.repro_detail:
I wrote a temporary probe, crates/ingest/tests/diag_void_1.rs, and ran it with the gate flags and package set plus `--test diag_void_1`: EXIT=0, `test result: ok`. It builds `store::Parsed` from the public `/content` of the 25 located notices (24 r208 and the text notice 3322691), records them in a scratch DB, runs the real `project::project` and lists the surviving mentions.

| Run | Fold report | Surviving void-net mentions |
|---|---|---|
| As published | mentions=130, dropped void=1, placeholder=127 (prod's 2353 line said 127 placeholder too) | 38, all with heads the walk re-queues |
| Same notices, only the ordinal-0 name copy kept | dropped void=39, placeholder=127 | 0 |

Every kept party printed its copy count, how many copies were void, and the unclassed copies. For example, 16893864 ORG-2 has 23 copies, 6 void and 17 unclassed ('Kontrakten ikke tildelt.', 'Der Auftrag wurde nicht vergeben.', 'El contrato no ha sido adjudicado.', …). 12501289 ORG-11 has 2 copies, 1 void and 1 unclassed ('Zuschlag nicht vergeben').

So the head copy alone is dropped, and the other-language copies are what keep the party.

The text notice: the fold keeps 3322691 ORG-2 'NO AWARD WAS MADE' as a mention. A direct check gave:
- `not_a_name('NO AWARD WAS MADE')` = None, `is_void_lot` false.
- `not_a_name('No award was made')` = VoidLot, `is_void_lot` true.

The probe is deleted, the scratch DBs are removed, and `git status` is empty.
diagnoses.fix:
Change the walk, not the fold. The fold is the authority, so the walk must predict the fold's decision for the whole party, not judge one name.

**What to change:**
- Expose the fold's own party decision. Add a public wrapper in crates/ingest/src/project.rs over `dropped_party_sections` / `drop_decision`, built from a notice's `Parsed` with the same sdk01 flag, section map and `nested_org_aliases` the fold uses (as at :5171).
- Give the store a mention read that returns `(org, notice, section)`. It is today's `mention_notices_of_orgs` plus `section_id`.
- In `run_refold_non_names`, after the unchanged `mentions_void` net:
  - read each hit notice through `parsed_by_ids`;
  - re-queue a mention only when the fold drops that section;
  - list the rest under `exempted` with a reason such as "kept by the fold's party rule (unclassed name copies)";
  - when a parse is missing or unreadable, re-queue anyway, so the re-queued set always covers the fold's drops.

**Why:**
- The re-queued set then equals the fold's drops inside the net, by construction. All 40 mentions (both classes, and the unlocated r209 one) move to `exempted`, and the drain stops re-queuing the same 26 notices every run.
- The net is untouched, so it is still a superset of what the walk re-queues.
- Nothing is written to the corpus.
- The docs' claim that the walk uses "the fold's own predicate" becomes true. Fix that line in docs/operations.md and the doc comment at supervisor.rs:3788-3791.

**Optional second step, a separate decision for the owner:** these 37 orgs really are void lots. Removing them would mean widening the fold, either by adding TED's template wordings to `VOID_WHOLE` and 'was' to `CONTINUATIONS` (or 'no award was made' as a whole value), or by adding a VoidLot translation echo modelled on 511 unit 4.
diagnoses.risk:
**Walk fix (recommended):**
- It cannot turn a real award into no-award, because the walk only chooses what to re-queue.
- Risk 1, drift: if the walk ever calls anything other than the fold's own `drop_decision` with the same inputs, its re-queued set could fall below the fold's drops. That is why it must reuse the function and re-queue whenever it can't decide.
- Risk 2, cost: one parse read per notice the net hits. That is 26 notices here and about 8.5k on a first-drain scale, chunked.
- Existing gap the fix does not close: the net still reads only the head name. Under the majority rule the fold can drop a party whose head copy is unclassed (a DE-original head such as 'Der Auftrag wurde nicht vergeben.' with at least 12 of 23 copies void). The walk's net would miss its standing mention, which is the reverse of what the walk must guarantee. None of the 40 is that shape. Closing it needs the net to read every copy, e.g. `organization_names`.

**Fold widening (optional):** this is the real risk of turning a real award into no-award.
- A void echo or a lower threshold would sweep a copy that actually names a company: a bilingual party with 'non aggiudicato' in one language and a supplier name without a legal form in the other (e.g. 'Siemens', 'Kier Construction'). That is the shape 511's unit-6 review refused for placeholders.
- The 7 bilingual 2-copy mentions are exactly that shape.
- Any echo seeded by a non-head copy also drops parties the head-only net cannot see, unless the net is widened at the same time.
- The narrow lexicon route has the lowest risk: TED's fixed translations of 'Lot/Contract not awarded' are never company names. 'was' in `CONTINUATIONS` could misread an all-caps company named like 'DESIERTO WAS …', which seems unlikely.

diagnoses.root_cause:
The walk and the fold answer different questions.

- **Walk.** It splits its net with `NonNames::Void.requeues(org.name)`, which is `partyname::is_void_lot` applied to ONE string: the organization's head name (the first copy seen, in the original language). That is a per-name test.
- **Fold.** `drop_decision` decides per party within one notice. It classes every name the party publishes in that notice (all TED language copies, with nested halves folded onto the outer section). It drops the party only if EVERY name is classed, or if the party has 4 or more names and at least half of them are VoidLot. It then retires recorded mentions by the OUTERMOST section key only.

`is_void_lot` documents itself as "the fold's rule, as a plain predicate", and operations.md says the walk uses "the fold's own predicate". Both claims are false here: the party-level step and the retire key are missing from the walk. Three classes result:

- **A, 38 of 40, all on r208.** TED multilingual winner slots where the head copy is void but most translations are not in VOID_WHOLE, so the fold keeps the party.
  - Bilingual IT/DE (South Tyrol), 7 mentions (12501289 ×5, 4416766 ×2): 'non aggiudicato' is VoidLot, 'Zuschlag nicht vergeben' is unclassed (VOID_WHOLE has only the whole value 'nicht vergeben'). That is 1 of 2 names; the all-names rule fails and n<4 rules out the majority rule.
  - 23 or 24 languages, 31 mentions: only 1 to 7 copies are void. VOID_WHOLE's translations come from one TED template ('Not awarded / Ikke tildelt / …', notice 17674598). The other templates ('Contract not awarded.' / 'Kontrakten ikke tildelt.' / 'Der Auftrag wurde nicht vergeben.'; 'No contract awarded.' / 'Ingen kontrakt tildelt.'; 'Lot not awarded'; 'Marché non attribué.'; 'Non applicable — …') miss most languages.
  - Notice 16967678 shows both outcomes at once: ORG-2 uses the old template (22 of 23 void) and is dropped; ORG-4 uses 'No contract awarded.' (7 of 23 void) and is kept.
- **C, 1 of 40, text notice 3322691 ORG-2.** The raw name is 'NO AWARD WAS MADE'; the org head 27220329 is the differently-cased 'No award was made'. `void_prefix` is case-sensitive: 'No award' followed by lowercase 'was' reads as void, but uppercase 'WAS' (not in CONTINUATIONS) reads as a possible company. The walk tests the head and gets true; the fold tests the raw name and gets None, so it keeps the party.
- **B, 1 of 40, r209 notice 23151933.** This is a true fold/store miss. ORG-2 (TED-WINNER, no name) contains nested ORG-3 (ADDRESS_WINNER, 'marché déclaré sans suite'). The fold drops the party (it is one of the 2353 report's "2 void"; the other is 16967678 ORG-2). Its drop map includes the inner half ORG-3, but the retire keys are outermost only. The recorded prod row sits at (23151933, ORG-3), the key issue 259's landing repair left in place; there is no ORG-2 row. `retire_mentions` looks up the exact key (23151933, ORG-2), finds nothing (hence "0 non-name retired"), and the inner row stays. The walk keeps listing it.

These parties survive every drain because the fold keeps 39 of them by its party rule, and cannot reach the 40th through the outer-only retire key.

diagnoses.fix:
Two minimal fixes, one per side, both keeping the walk's re-queue set a superset of what the fold drops.

**1. Walk side, for A and C (39 of 40).** The fold's keep is its documented design, and changing it would change drops across the whole r208 corpus, so the walk is what must change. `NonNames::Void.requeues(head)` (supervisor.rs:3794) is only the per-name half of the fold's rule.
- Expose the fold's own decision from ingest::project, e.g. `pub fn dropped_sections(profile, &Parsed) -> BTreeMap<String, NotAName>`: `drop_decision` plus the inner aliases, i.e. exactly `decision.sections`.
- In `run_refold_non_names`, for each net hit:
  - read its mention `(notice, section)` pairs (`organization_mentions` has `section_id`) and the notices' parsed rows (`parsed_by_ids`; the net is about 412 orgs, so a few hundred notices);
  - re-queue a notice only when the mention's section is in that map with the walk's class;
  - list net hits the fold keeps under `exempted`, with the reason (e.g. 'party kept: 6/23 names void').
- Because the walk and the fold then call the same function, the re-queue set equals the fold's drops on recorded mentions. The dry count converges to 0 after a drain instead of re-listing these 26 notices forever.
- To stay a superset, widen the net to the org's `organization_names` variants, not only the head. Otherwise a party whose head copy is unclassed but which the majority rule drops (e.g. a DE-original TED notice) is never seen.
- Fix operations.md:1755 to match.

**2. Fold side, for B (1 of 40).** Hand retirement every key of `decision.sections`, outer plus inner halves.
- In `mentions_and_dropped` (project.rs:5291-5296), return a retire list without the `!alias.contains_key` filter.
- Keep that filter for minting and counting (`DroppedParties` reads `decision.outer` already).
- This flows through 2192 and 3216 into `retire_mentions`, which is already a no-op for keys with no recorded row.

**Optional data-quality follow-up (fold side; needs its own decision and drain).** The 37 orgs are genuinely void. If they should go, add the other TED template copies and the South Tyrol pair to VOID_WHOLE as whole values: 'zuschlag nicht vergeben', 'appalto non aggiudicato', 'der auftrag wurde nicht vergeben', 'kontrakten ikke tildelt', 'el contrato no ha sido adjudicado', 'contrato nao adjudicado', 'ingen kontrakt tildelt', 'no award was made', and so on. An alternative is a VoidLot translation echo modelled on 511's `translation_echoes`. With either, fix 1 lists them as re-queues automatically.
diagnoses.risk:
**Fix 1 (walk side) changes no data.** It only shrinks what is re-queued to what the fold will actually retire.
- Its one hazard is under-listing: if the net stays head-only, or the shared function is called with the wrong sdk01/profile flag, a party the fold would drop is never re-queued. Mitigations:
  - reuse `Ident::read`'s sdk01 decision;
  - widen the net to the `organization_names` variants;
  - add a test asserting `walk_requeued ⊇ fold_dropped` over fixtures that include the 16967678 pair (ORG-2 dropped, ORG-4 kept) and the nested 23151933 shape.
- Cost: one `parsed_by_ids` read per net-hit notice (a few hundred), which is negligible.

**Fix 2 (inner-key retire) is low risk.** Inner halves are the same party by the fold's own read, and `NoticeState::read` already drops roles through them. Retire is a no-op without a recorded row. Its effects:
- It deletes party and bid-party rows keyed to the inner mention, with D5 corrections already announced.
- It stamps the affected Tenders stale.
- It can retire other issue-259-repaired inner mentions of void, placeholder or blank parties corpus-wide. Size it with a dry walk first (fix 1 lists them).

**The optional fold-lexicon change carries the real award-to-no-award risk.**
- Whole-value VOID_WHOLE additions are safe-ish: exact equality on a winner slot, and no company is named 'Zuschlag nicht vergeben'. Avoid stems.
- Never relax the 2-name all-void rule: a bilingual FI/SV or IT/DE award with one void copy and one company copy must stay a party.
- Do not make `void_prefix` case-blind, or 'DESIERTO OÜ'-style company names fall. Use whole values like 'no award was made' instead.
- A translation echo must be seeded only by a bare VoidLot whole value. It may sweep only short copies with no legal form, a different language label and no award clause.
- These also feed the text parser and the walk's net, so run a dry census of newly-void parties with identifiers or legal forms before any drain.

verdict.root_cause:
Diagnosis 2 is right and accounts for all 40 mentions. Diagnosis 1 explains 39 correctly but gets the 40th wrong. There are two separate causes.

(1) The walk and the fold judge different things: 39 of 40.
- **Walk:** it splits its net with `NonNames::requeues`. That calls `ingest::partyname::is_void_lot(name)` (crates/app/src/supervisor.rs:3794) on `organizations.name` alone, the head name, applied at supervisor.rs:5581 (`if class.requeues(&org.1)`). That is the fold's rule for one name.
- **Fold:** `drop_decision` (crates/ingest/src/project.rs:4504) collects every published name copy of the party in that notice (:4522-4538), nested halves included. It drops the party only in two cases:
  - every copy is classed (:4548), or
  - there are 4 or more copies and at least half are VoidLot (:4556).
  Otherwise it keeps the party (`continue`, :4559). The echo passes (`translation_echoes` / `template_echoes`, :4664/:4725) only spread Placeholder, never VoidLot.

That gives two classes.
- **Class A, 38 mentions, all 24 ted-export-r208 notices.** TED multilingual winner slots where the head copy is void but most copies are other TED wordings that `VOID_WHOLE` (partyname.rs:141) does not hold.
  - Notice 12501289 ORG-11 (and the other 4 ORG sections on it) has 2 copies: IT 'non aggiudicato' and DE 'Zuschlag nicht vergeben'. With 2 copies the majority rule never applies.
  - Notice 16893864 ORG-2 has 23 copies, about 6 of them void: 'Kontrakten ikke tildelt.', 'Der Auftrag wurde nicht vergeben.', 'Appalto non aggiudicato.', …
  - I re-fetched both from /content and confirmed the shapes.
- **Class C, 1 mention, text notice 3322691 ORG-2.** On the box the mention name is 'NO AWARD WAS MADE'; the head of org 27220329 is 'No award was made'. `void_prefix` treats a lowercase next word as part of the void phrase (partyname.rs:2500, `first.is_lowercase()`), and 'was' is not in `CONTINUATIONS`.
  - The head reads VoidLot, so the walk re-queues it.
  - The raw all-caps name reads as a name, so the fold keeps it.

(2) A real defect in the fold's retire path, class B: 1 of 40, the r209 notice 23151933. Diagnosis 1 left this one unlocated and guessed "multi-copy", which is wrong.
- **Shape.** ORG-2 is the TED-WINNER and has no name. ORG-3, the address-winner, sits inside it with the single name 'marché déclaré sans suite'.
- **The fold drops the party.** It is one of 2353's "2 void"; the other is 16967678 ORG-2. Diagnosis 1's 25-notice probe got void=1 and Diagnosis 2's 26-notice probe got 2, which corroborates this. `decision.sections` includes the inner half ORG-3.
- **But only the outer key is retired.** The keys handed to retirement keep outer sections only: project.rs:5294 filters on `!alias.contains_key(&s.id) && void.contains_key(&s.id)`. `retire_mentions` (crates/store/src/canonical.rs:19343) then looks up the exact (notice, section) pair and skips it when no row exists.
- **The box has the row at the inner key.** A bounded read shows (23151933, ORG-3) → org 1265984 'marché déclaré sans suite' is recorded and there is no ORG-2 row. That is the layout issue 259's landing repair leaves behind.
- **Result.** The walk re-queues the notice, the fold drops the party and retires nothing ("0 non-name retired"), and the walk lists it again next time.
verdict.why:
Checked against the code:
- **Walk:** supervisor.rs:3794 and :5581, plus `mention_notices_of_orgs`, re-queue every notice that has a mention of an org whose head name passes.
- **Fold:** the rules at project.rs:4548 and :4556; both echo passes are Placeholder-only.
- **Retire keys:** the outer-only filter at project.rs:5294, which is the only source of the keys used at :2190/:2261 (full fold) and :3214/:3462 (incremental); `retire_mentions` looks up the exact key.

Checked against the box (bounded SELECT):

verdict.fix:
Two minimal changes, one per side. Both keep the fold as the authority and leave the walk's re-queued set covering every fold drop.

1. **Walk side, classes A and C (39 mentions).** The fold keeps these by its documented party rule, so the walk changes and the fold does not.
   - Expose the fold's decision from ingest::project: a public wrapper over `dropped_party_sections` / `drop_decision`, i.e. `decision.sections` with inner halves included. Build it from the notice's `Parsed` with the same sdk01 flag (`Ident::read`), section map and `nested_org_aliases` that `mentions_and_dropped` uses.
   - Give the store a mention read that returns (org, notice, section): `mention_notices_of_orgs` plus `section_id`.
   - In `run_refold_non_names`, keep the `mentions_void` net unchanged. Load the hit notices with `parsed_by_ids`, and re-queue a mention only when its (notice, section) is in the fold's drop map with the class being walked.
   - List the other hits under `exempted`, with the reason (e.g. 'party kept: 6/23 names void').
   - Re-queue whenever the parse is missing or unreadable.
   - Fix the "fold's own predicate" wording at supervisor.rs:3788-3791 and in docs/operations.md (refold-void-names section).
   - Recommended hardening, separate from the 40: widen the net to every `organization_names` copy of the org, not only the head. The majority rule can drop a party whose head copy is unclassed (a DE-original TED notice), and a head-only net never sees it.

2. **Fold side, class B (1 mention).** In `NoticeState::mentions_and_dropped` (project.rs:5292-5297), build the retire-key list (`skipped`) from every party section in `decision.sections`, inner aliases included: drop the `!alias.contains_key(&s.id)` term for `skipped` only. Minting (the `mentions` filter) and counting (`DroppedParties` from `decision.outer`) stay as they are. The keys flow unchanged through :2190 and :3214 into `retire_mentions`, which writes nothing for a key with no row. Update the unit tests that assert `skipped` for nested shapes.

With both changes:
- The 39 A/C mentions move to `exempted`.
- 23151933 ORG-3 is re-queued once and retired, and `sweep-orphan-orgs` can then remove org 1265984.
- The dry walk drops to 0 instead of re-listing these 26 notices after every drain.

Optional, needs its own decision and drain: the 37 orgs really are void lots. To actually remove them, widen the fold's lexicon with whole values only, e.g. 'zuschlag nicht vergeben', 'appalto non aggiudicato', 'der auftrag wurde nicht vergeben', 'kontrakten ikke tildelt', 'el contrato no ha sido adjudicado', 'no award was made'. Fix 1 then lists them as re-queues automatically.
verdict.risk:
**Fix 1 (walk side)** writes nothing to the corpus and cannot turn a real award into no-award; it only narrows what the walk re-queues.
- Its hazard is listing too little: if the wrapper is called with a different sdk01/profile flag, section map or alias map than the fold uses, a party the fold drops could be exempted. Mitigations:
  - call the same `drop_decision` with the same inputs;
  - re-queue whenever the walk cannot decide;
  - add a test that the re-queued set covers every fold drop, over fixtures including 16967678 (ORG-2 dropped at 22/23 void, ORG-4 kept at 7/23) and the nested 23151933 shape.
- Cost: one `parsed_by_ids` read per notice the net hits, chunked. That is 26 notices here and a few hundred to low thousands on a first drain.
- Until the net is widened, the existing head-only gap remains (a majority-rule drop whose head copy is unclassed). None of the 40 has that shape.

**Fix 2 (inner-key retire)** adds no new drop decision: the inner names were already in the party's tally, and `NoticeState::read` already drops roles through the inner half. It only carries out a drop the fold has already decided. Its effects:
- It deletes the stale mention row and any party or bid-party rows keyed to it, announces ADR-0017 D5 corrections (normally none, since the rows are already gone), and marks the affected Tenders stale.
- Corpus-wide, it will also retire other inner-key mentions left by the issue-259 repair whose parties are dropped as void, placeholder or blank, whenever their notices are refolded. A full fold could retire a batch of these at once.
- Size it before deploying: dry-count recorded mentions whose section is a nested Organization inside a dropped outer party. Then drain and run `sweep-orphan-orgs`.

**The optional lexicon widening** is where a real award could turn into no-award.
- Keep it to whole values only, never stems.
- Never relax the 2-copy rule that every copy must be classed: a bilingual IT/DE or FI/SV award with one void copy and one company name must stay a party.
- Do not make `void_prefix` case-blind, or company names of the 'DESIERTO OÜ' kind would be dropped.
- Any VoidLot echo must be seeded by a bare whole value and must exclude copies with a legal form.
- Run a dry census of newly void parties that carry identifiers or legal forms before draining. The same lexicon also feeds the text parser and the walk's net.
